correctness.rationale: The exact polynomial follows from independently checked conditional factorial moments (k)_r(l)_r/(n)_r² for common occupied matrix entries, and D=K+L-2C. Complete direct enumeration agrees for n=1..4, while n=10,20,40 coefficient/normalization checks replay. The joint limit follows from the classical locally uniform Laguerre Perron expansion (Gaussian deficiencies), dominated conditional pgf convergence to exp(t-1) (Poisson one, independent), and an exact distance identity plus the delta method. No finite enumeration is misrepresented as proof of the asymptotic theorem.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge non-coverage after literal and alias/equivalence published-finding corpus searches, own ledger claim inspection, full-text checks of Heuer–Striker, Torres, Gouyou-Beauchamps–Nicaud, and the two closest published uniform-rook results. Priority remains provisional because an unindexed equivalent may exist.
residual_risks: An unindexed Hamming-distance polynomial or random rook-position coincidence theorem could cover part or all of the distance formula; full historical uniqueness is not certified.
The univariate Gaussian rank-deficiency limit and exact one-vertex covariance are prior results; neither is claimed as new.
The conditional common-edge law is tied to the full square board; no claim for rectangular or graph-constrained matchings.

value.rationale: The complete Frobenius vertex-pair distance distribution is a natural metric invariant of the classical doubly substochastic polytope, not a parameter-engineered finite slice. The independent discrete Poisson correction provides information erased by first-order Gaussian distance fluctuations and distinguishes shared-edge geometry from pure rank effects. It is an all-dimensional exact polynomial plus a meaningful two-scale limit, not merely a low-order moment or standard enumeration.
